transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Gritty, sandy bits left on glasses and bowls are a common sign of a clogged filter in the bottom of the tub. When it's blocked, the machine keeps recirculating dirty water and sprays the grit back onto the dishes. That's by far the most common cause, and it's a free fix. Next most likely are blocked spray-arm jets or an arm that's being stopped from turning, and less often a quick or eco programme that isn't strong enough. With the machine switched off, try these in order: 1. Clean the filter. Pull out the lower rack, then twist and lift out the filter assembly in the base of the tub (usually a cylinder with a flat mesh plate around it). Rinse both under the tap, using a soft brush on the mesh, and wipe out any debris from the sump underneath. Watch for broken glass. If it was full of food or grit, that's probably your problem. Refit it so it locks down fully. 2. Check the spray arms. Spin each one by hand: they should turn freely. Look at the little jet holes. Most arms unclip, so you can rinse them and poke out any blocked holes with a cocktail stick. A stuck arm or blocked jets would explain weak washing, especially if one rack or area is worse than the others. 3. Check the loading. With a normal load in, spin the arms again. Tall pans, trays or a dangling utensil can stop an arm turning, which gives patchy results. 4. Run a normal or intensive programme, not quick or eco, with a typical load and see if the dishes come out clean. If they're still gritty after a clean filter and clear arms, the next thing to look at is whether the machine is heating and actually spraying during the wash: is it hot and steamy when you open it at the end, and can you hear water sloshing? That would point towards the less common internal causes. How did the filter look when you got it out?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

ok did the filter, it was full of food n grease. checked the spray arms too, lower one spins fine but upper one is stiff. several holes on the upper arm were blocked with seeds/limescale, cleared them with a cocktail stick. ran a normal programme after and its much better

That's sorted, then. A filter full of food and grease explains the gritty bits: the machine was spraying dirty water back over the dishes. The blocked jets on the top arm would have made the upper rack worse too. To stop it coming back:
1. Rinse the filter every couple of weeks, or weekly if you use the machine a lot. Scrape plates into the bin rather than leaving big bits on.
2. The limescale in the jets suggests hard water, so keep the dishwasher salt and rinse aid topped up. Every month or two, run an empty hot wash with a dishwasher cleaner or descaler.
3. Try spinning the upper arm by hand again now it's clean. If it still feels stiff or wobbly, unclip it, rinse the hub where it mounts and refit it so it seats properly. If it still drags after that, the arm or its mounting may be worn and worth replacing, as a stiff arm won't cover the top rack properly. Is there anything else I can help with?
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
